def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-:
## Definition

Let the representable set, normal range, and unit roundoff be as in [[def-standard-relative-floating-point-model-and-unit-roundoff]]. Here fl is round-to-nearest, ties-to-even, on each real exact result that is zero or normal; every other nonzero exact result (subnormal or overflow), NaN, infinity, invalid operation, or division by zero returns range-failure. A real add, subtract, multiply, or divide is one rounded operation. For positive in-range x, fl(sqrt(x)) is correctly rounded to nearest, ties-to-even, and fails unless its result is positive and normal. A real fused multiply-add returns the correctly rounded value of the single exact expression ab+c; it is not two operations.

Complex addition and subtraction round real and imaginary components separately. A complex product (a+ib)(c+id) uses four rounded real products ac, bd, ad, bc, then rounded subtraction and addition, for six real operations. Conjugation and sign changes are exact. Scaling and division by a positive real scalar round each complex component separately; no other complex division primitive is used here.

A procedure succeeds only when each exact intermediate is zero or normal and every rounded output is finite; otherwise it returns the first range-failure with its operation or pivot index. For ku<1 write gamma_k=ku/(1-ku). This is a no-underflow success model, not the gradual-underflow model.
alg-balanced-pairwise-summation:
## Definition

Input real floating-point x_1,...,x_n, n>=1. Set d=ceil(log_2 n), append 2^d-n exact zero leaves, and round the sum at each internal node of the balanced tree. An unmatched leaf may be copied. If a rounded node fails the operationwise range rule, return range-failure and its tree index; otherwise return the root s-hat. This finite tree terminates after 2^d-1 additions; accuracy is asserted only on success.
alg-two-sum-error-free-transform:
## Definition

For real floating-point a,b compute s=fl(a+b), z=fl(s-a), e=fl((a-(s-z))+(b-z)), with every operation separately rounded. Return the first range failure and operation index if an exact intermediate is nonzero subnormal, overflowed, or otherwise invalid; otherwise return (s,e). The fixed sequence terminates. Its general exact-transform claim is a separate theorem; this definition alone does not prove exact recovery.
alg-two-product-fma-error-free-transform:
## Definition

For real floating-point a,b compute p=fl(ab), then e=fma(a,b,-p). Return range-failure if the product overflows, the exact FMA residual is nonzero subnormal or overflow, or another operationwise range condition fails; otherwise return (p,e). The procedure uses one multiplication and one fused multiply-add and terminates. Exact recovery is claimed only if ab-p is representable as zero or a normal number.
alg-kahan-compensated-summation:
## Definition

For real floating-point inputs $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, initialize s_0=c_0=0. For i=1,...,n compute y_i=fl(x_i-c_{i-1}), s_i=fl(s_{i-1}+y_i), d_i=fl(s_i-s_{i-1}), c_i=fl(d_i-y_i), in that order. Return s_n, or the first range-failure and its operation index. There are 4n rounded operations, so the finite loop terminates. Its data-dependent error identity is proved separately.
alg-neumaier-compensated-summation:
## Definition

For real floating-point inputs $x_1,\ldots,x_n$ initialize s_0=c_0=0. Set t_i=fl(s_{i-1}+x_i). If |s_{i-1}|>=|x_i| set q_i=fl(s_{i-1}-t_i), a_i=fl(q_i+x_i); otherwise set q_i=fl(x_i-t_i), a_i=fl(q_i+s_{i-1}). Then set c_i=fl(c_{i-1}+a_i), s_i=t_i. Return fl(s_n+c_n), or the first range-failure and operation index. The branch test is defined for all real inputs and the loop terminates.
alg-rounded-cholesky-with-failure-status:
## Definition

Input a Hermitian positive-definite matrix $A\in\mathbb C^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, whose real and imaginary components are in the floating-point system, in the convention of [[def-cholesky-factorisation-with-positive-diagonal]]; real matrices are included. Set L-hat=0. For j=1,...,n, form the diagonal sum from rounded real squares of the real and imaginary components of l_jk and rounded additions, then p_j=fl(a_jj-sum_{k<j}|l_jk|^2). If an operation fails or p_j is not positive normal, return failure(j). Set l_jj=fl(sqrt(p_j)); unless this is positive normal return failure(j). For i>j, form c_ij by sequential complex products with six real operations each and componentwise rounded additions; form r_ij=fl(a_ij-c_ij) componentwise and divide each real component by positive l_jj with one rounded real division. Any range failure returns failure(j) with the operation index. If all columns finish, return success(L-hat). The loops are finite. By [[thm-cholesky-factorisation-exists-iff-hermitian-positive-definite-and-is-unique]], exact positive definiteness ensures an exact factor exists, but does not ensure the rounded algorithm succeeds.
alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formati:
## Definition

Input a real active column $x\in\mathbb F^r$ and trailing block $B\in\mathbb F^{r\times q}$, with entries in the floating-point system, $r\ge1$, and $q\ge0$. If $x=0$, return the identity action and copy $B$. Otherwise let $s=\max_i|x_i|>0$, compute $z_i=\operatorname{fl}(x_i/s)$ and $t=\operatorname{fl}(\sum_i z_i^2)$ by sequential rounded operations, then $\widehat r=\operatorname{fl}(s\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt t))$. Set $\sigma=1$ when $x_1=0$ and $\sigma=\operatorname{sign}(x_1)$ otherwise, $\widehat\alpha=-\sigma\widehat r$, $v_i=\operatorname{fl}(x_i-\widehat\alpha\,1_{i=1})$, $w=\operatorname{fl}(v^Tv)$, and $\widehat\tau=\operatorname{fl}(2/w)$. Compute $d=\operatorname{fl}(v^TB)$ by sequential rounded products and additions, $p_i=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat\tau v_i)$, $U_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}(p_i d_j)$, and $\widehat B_{ij}=\operatorname{fl}(B_{ij}-U_{ij})$. The complete active output is $C_+=[\widehat\alpha e_1\;\widehat B]$: write exact zeros below its first diagonal entry. This fixes the multiplication order and includes the column overwrite in the analyzed step. Return the first range failure on any invalid or out-of-range operation; return failure if $t$, $\widehat r$, or $w$ is not positive normal, or any intermediate is nonfinite. Otherwise return $(v,\widehat\tau,\widehat\alpha,C_+)$. Store these reflectors to represent the exact orthogonal product; a rounded explicit dense product is a separate output with its own arithmetic error. The exact reflector associated with nonzero stored $v$ is $H(v)=I-2vv^T/(v^Tv)$, using [[def-householder-reflector]] and the QR convention of [[def-full-reduced-and-column-pivoted-computational-qr-factorisations]]. This definition does not assert a local backward-error bound.
alg-bounded-mixed-precision-iterative-re:
## Definition

Input nonsingular real $A\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$, $n\ge1$, and $b,x_0\in\mathbb R^n$, nonsingular factor matrix $\widehat A$ formed at factorization precision $u_f$, residual precision $u_r$, solve/update precision $u_w$, finite budget $N\ge0$, tolerance $\tau\ge0$, certified nonnegative constants $\eta_r,\xi_r,\eta_w,\xi_w$, and a certified contraction upper bound $0\le q_{\mathrm{cert}}<1$. Let $x_*=A^{-1}b$ be the unique exact solution. Use the operationwise model of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]] separately at $u_f,u_r,u_w$. The exact data $A,b$ are available to residual evaluation at $u_r$; stored iterates and correction updates use $u_w$. At iteration $k$, compute $\widehat r_k=\operatorname{fl}_{u_r}(b-Ax_k)$, solve for a correction using the supplied triangular factors of $\widehat A$ and the recurrence in [[def-forward-and-back-substitution-for-triangular-systems]], then round $x_{k+1}=\operatorname{fl}_{u_w}(x_k+\widehat z_k)$. A certificate must bound the residual defect $\widehat r_k=A(x_*-x_k)+\delta_{r,k}$ by $\|\delta_{r,k}\|_2\le\eta_r(\|A\|_2\|x_k\|_2+\|b\|_2)+\xi_r$, and the combined solve/update residual-equivalent error is defined by
$$x_{k+1}=x_k+\widehat A^{-1}(\widehat r_k+\delta_{w,k}),\qquad \|\delta_{w,k}\|_2\le\eta_w\|\widehat r_k\|_2+\xi_w.$$
The certificate must verify that $q\le q_{\mathrm{cert}}$, where
$$q=\|I-\widehat A^{-1}A\|_2+ \|\widehat A^{-1}\|_2((1+\eta_w)\eta_r+\eta_w)\|A\|_2.$$
If a required range or nonsingularity check fails, a certificate is unavailable, or $q\le q_{\mathrm{cert}}<1$ is not certified, return inconclusive. Otherwise test the current residual, return residual-tolerance if its computed norm is at most $\tau$, and update at most $N$ times; return budget-exhausted after $N$ unsuccessful updates. Return the current iterate with its status. The procedure is finite and does not claim exact termination or unconditional convergence.
thm-balanced-pairwise-summation-error-bo:
## Statement

Let $x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb R$, $n\ge1$, be successfully processed by [[alg-balanced-pairwise-summation]] in the operationwise model. Put $d=\lceil\log_2 n\rceil$, assume $du<1$, and set $\gamma_d=du/(1-du)$. Then
$$\left|\widehat s-\sum_{i=1}^n x_i\right|\le\gamma_d\sum_{i=1}^n|x_i|.$$
For $n=1$, $d=0$ and the error is zero.
lem-binary-rounding-grid-and-ordered-two:
## Statement

For an integer $p\ge2$, let $\mathbb B_p=\{0\}\cup\{\pm m2^k: m,k\in\mathbb Z,\ 2^{p-1}\le m<2^p\}$, with unbounded exponent. Let $R$ round a real number to its nearest member of $\mathbb B_p$, breaking ties by the even normalized significand; set $R(0)=0$. For $x\ne0$ put $E(x)$ be the unique integer with $2^{E(x)}\le|x|<2^{E(x)+1}$, and set $q(x)=2^{E(x)-p+1}$. The following hold.

- $R$ is monotone, odd, and fixes $\mathbb B_p$. For $R(t)\ne0$, $|R(t)-t|\le q(R(t))/2$.
- If $x,y\in\mathbb B_p$, then $\rho=R(x+y)-(x+y)$ belongs to $\mathbb B_p$ and $|\rho|\le\min(|x|,|y|)$. If $|R(x+y)|<\min(|x|,|y|)$, the sum is exact.
- If $x,y\in\mathbb B_p$ have the same sign and $|x|/2\le|y|\le2|x|$, then $x-y\in\mathbb B_p$ (Sterbenz exact subtraction).
- If $A,B\in\mathbb B_p$ and $|A|\ge|B|$, then $S=R(A+B)$, $Z=R(S-A)$, $T=R(B-Z)$ satisfy $Z=S-A$ and $T=A+B-S$ exactly.
thm-two-sum-error-free-transform:
## Statement

Use a binary floating-point format of precision $p\ge2$: its normal positive values are $m2^{j-p+1}$ for integers $2^{p-1}\le m<2^p$ and $e_{\min}\le j\le e_{\max}$, with their negatives and zero. Any additional representable values below the normal range must belong to the unbounded binary set $\mathbb B_p$ of [[lem-binary-rounding-grid-and-ordered-two-sum]] (as ordinary binary subnormals do). Round each operation to nearest, ties to even, with the no-underflow success rule of [[def-operationwise-real-complex-floating-point-model-with-sqrt-and-fma]].

For any representable real inputs $a,b$ for which [[alg-two-sum-error-free-transform]] succeeds, its output satisfies
$$s=\operatorname{fl}(a+b),\qquad e=(a+b)-s,\qquad s+e=a+b$$
exactly in real arithmetic. No ordering or sign condition on the inputs is required; zeros, exact cancellation, and all successful calls at either normal-range boundary are included.
thm-two-product-fma-error-free-transform:
## Statement

Let $a,b$ be real floating-point numbers successfully processed by [[alg-two-product-fma-error-free-transform]], and assume the exact residual $ab-p$ is representable as zero or a normal number. Then the returned pair satisfies $p+e=ab$ exactly.
thm-kahan-and-neumaier-finite-error-iden:
## Statement

For successfully processed real inputs $x_1,\ldots,x_n$, let $\epsilon_i^y,\epsilon_i^s,\epsilon_i^d,\epsilon_i^c$ be the signed errors in the four Kahan operations. Then
$$s_n-\sum_{i=1}^n x_i=\sum_{i=1}^n\epsilon_i^y+\epsilon_n^s-\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}(\epsilon_i^d+\epsilon_i^c),$$
hence
$$|s_n-\sum_i x_i|\le u\sum_i|x_i-c_{i-1}|+u|s_{n-1}+y_n|+u\sum_{i<n}(|s_i-s_{i-1}|+|d_i-y_i|).$$
For Neumaier, let $\epsilon_i^t,\epsilon_i^q,\epsilon_i^a,\epsilon_i^c$ be the signed errors at the actually executed operations and $\epsilon^f$ the final rounding error. Then
$$\widehat s-\sum_i x_i=\sum_i(\epsilon_i^t+\epsilon_i^q+\epsilon_i^a+\epsilon_i^c)+\epsilon^f.$$
For each $i$, define $P_i$ by the branch-specific expression below. Then
$$|\widehat s-\sum_i x_i|\le u\sum_iP_i+u|s_n+c_n|,$$
where the final term accounts for the last rounded addition. These are finite data-dependent bounds, not uniform relative-error claims.

$$P_i=|s_{i-1}|+|x_i|+ \begin{cases}|s_{i-1}|+|t_i|,&|s_{i-1}|\ge|x_i|,\\|x_i|+|t_i|,&|s_{i-1}|<|x_i|\end{cases} +\begin{cases}|q_i|+|x_i|,&|s_{i-1}|\ge|x_i|,\\|q_i|+|s_{i-1}|,&|s_{i-1}|<|x_i|\end{cases} +|c_{i-1}|+|a_i|.$$
thm-rounded-cholesky-componentwise-and-n:
## Statement

Let $n\ge1$ and let $A=A^*$ be positive definite in $\mathbb C^{n\times n}$. Suppose the rounded Cholesky algorithm succeeds with $\widehat L$. Put $m=20n+20$ and $g=\gamma_m=\frac{m u}{1-m u}$; assume $m u<1/5$. For $E=\widehat L\widehat L^*-A$, which is Hermitian, and with $|M|$ denoting entrywise absolute value for matrices,
$$|E|\le100g\,|\widehat L|\,|\widehat L|^*\quad\hbox{entrywise},\qquad \|E\|_F\le100g\|\widehat L\|_F^2,\qquad \|E\|_2\le100g\|\widehat L\|_F^2.$$
Thus $c_n(u)u=\frac{100m u}{1-m u}$. If also $100\sqrt n\,g\le1/2$, then
$$\|E\|_F\le200\sqrt n\,g\|A\|_F,\qquad \|E\|_2\le200\sqrt n\,g\|A\|_F.$$
These bounds apply on success only; positive definiteness does not guarantee rounded success.
lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-:
## Statement

Let $C=[x\;B]\in\mathbb R^{r\times(q+1)}$, $r\ge1$, $q\ge0$, undergo a successful step of [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]], with $0<u<1$ and $ru<1$. Define
$$g_r=\frac{ru}{1-ru},\quad e_r=(1+u)^{r/2+3}-1,\quad d_r=e_r+u(2+e_r),\quad a_r=\frac{1+u}{(1-u)^r}-1,$$
$$c_r=2\bigl((1+a_r)(1+u)^2(1+g_r)-1\bigr),\qquad \kappa_r=\max\{e_r+8d_r,(1+u)c_r+3u\}.$$
There is an exact orthogonal $H$, the identity when $x=0$ and $H(v)=I-2vv^T/(v^Tv)$ otherwise, and a perturbation $E$ such that
$$H(C+E)=C_+,\qquad \|E\|_F\le\kappa_r\|C\|_F.$$
The constants increase with $r$ and are $O(ru)$ for fixed $r$ as $u\to0$. The column overwrite is included. For successful application of the same stored $(v,\widehat\tau)$ to a separate block $Y$ without an annihilation overwrite, the discrepancy from $H(v)Y$ is at most $((1+u)c_r+3u)\|Y\|_F$.
thm-mixed-precision-refinement-error-rec:
## Statement

Let A be nonsingular, Ax_*=b, A-hat nonsingular, and e_k=x_*-x_k. Suppose the successful refinement algorithm has r-hat_k=Ae_k+delta_r,k with ||delta_r,k||_2<=eta_r(||A||_2||x_k||_2+||b||_2)+xi_r and combined solve/update residual-equivalent error ||delta_w,k||_2<=eta_w||r-hat_k||_2+xi_w. Set rho_0=xi_r+eta_r(||A||_2||x_*||_2+||b||_2),
q=||I-A-hat^{-1}A||_2+||A-hat^{-1}||_2((1+eta_w)eta_r+eta_w)||A||_2,
eta=||A-hat^{-1}||_2((1+eta_w)rho_0+xi_w).
Then e_{k+1}=(I-A-hat^{-1}A)e_k-A-hat^{-1}(delta_r,k+delta_w,k). If q<1 then ||e_k||_2<=q^k||e_0||_2+eta(1-q^k)/(1-q) for every executed k<=N. The precision floor is eta/(1-q); this is conditional and does not promise exact termination.
thm-scaled-householder-qr-backward-stabi:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $m\ge n\ge1$, undergo successful QR steps of [[alg-scaled-householder-reflector-formation-and-application]], with $mu<1$. Use $\kappa_m$ from [[lem-scaled-householder-step-meets-local-backward-error-premise]] and set $\beta_Q=(1+\kappa_m)^n-1$. The exact orthogonal product represented by the stored reflectors has reduced first $n$ columns $\widehat Q$, and the computed triangular block is $\widehat R$. Then
$$A+\Delta A=\widehat Q\widehat R,\qquad \|\Delta A\|_F\le\beta_Q\|A\|_F.$$
Applying the stored reflectors in the same order to a separate vector $b$, by their rounded rank-one updates without column overwrites, gives a full vector $\widehat c$ satisfying
$$\|\widehat c-Q_{\rm full}^Tb\|_2\le\beta_Q\|b\|_2.$$
The bounds are $O(u)$ for fixed dimensions. An explicitly rounded dense product for $Q_{\rm full}$ is not asserted exactly orthogonal.
thm-computed-full-rank-least-squares-bac:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $m\ge n\ge1$, have full column rank. Successful scaled Householder QR gives the exactly orthonormal reduced representative $\widehat Q$ and computed triangular $\widehat R$ with
$$A+\Delta_Q=\widehat Q\widehat R,\qquad \|\Delta_Q\|_F\le\beta_Q\|A\|_F,\qquad \beta_Q=(1+\kappa_m)^n-1,$$
where $\kappa_m$ is the proved local-step coefficient. Apply the stored reflectors to $b$ by rounded rank-one updates and let $\widehat y$ be the first $n$ coordinates. Set $\beta_b=\beta_Q$. Alternatively, if an explicitly supplied exactly orthonormal $\widehat Q$ has entries admissible as arithmetic inputs and $\widehat y=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat Q^Tb)$ uses sequential rounded dots, set $\beta_b=\sqrt n\,\gamma_m$. Solve $\widehat R\widehat x=\widehat y$ by successful rounded back substitution. Suppose $mu<1$ and $\gamma_{n+3}<1/8$. There exist $\delta b$ and upper triangular $\Delta R$ with
$$(\widehat R+\Delta R)\widehat x=\widehat Q^T(b+\delta b),\qquad \|\delta b\|_2\le\beta_b\|b\|_2,\qquad \|\Delta R\|_F\le\gamma_{n+3}\|\widehat R\|_F.$$
If $\widehat R+\Delta R$ is nonsingular, $\widehat x$ is the unique least-squares solution for $\widetilde A=\widehat Q(\widehat R+\Delta R)$ and $\widetilde b=b+\delta b$. The relative matrix perturbation is at most $\beta_Q+\gamma_{n+3}(1+\beta_Q)$; the right-hand perturbation is at most $\beta_b$. Consequently the formerly stated weaker factor $20\gamma_{n+3}$ bound also holds. Success and nonsingularity are explicit hypotheses.
lem-rounded-triangular-substitution-comp:
## Statement

Let $R\in\mathbb R^{n\times n}$ be upper triangular with nonzero diagonal, $y\in\mathbb R^n$, $n\ge1$, and $(n+3)u<1$. Compute descending substitution by the sequential rounded dot $s_i=\operatorname{fl}(\sum_{j>i}R_{ij}\widehat x_j)$ (empty sum zero), $t_i=\operatorname{fl}(y_i-s_i)$, and $\widehat x_i=\operatorname{fl}(t_i/R_{ii})$. If every operation succeeds, there is upper triangular $\Delta R$ with
$$(R+\Delta R)\widehat x=y,\qquad |\Delta R|\le\gamma_{n+3}|R|,\qquad \|\Delta R\|_F\le\gamma_{n+3}\|R\|_F.$$
In particular $\widehat x=0$ forces $y=0$. Forward substitution has the transposed conclusion.
lem-rounded-linear-and-normal-residual-c:
## Statement

Let $A\in\mathbb F^{m\times n}$, $x\in\mathbb F^n$, $y\in\mathbb F^m$ have stored real or complex entries, with $m,n\ge1$. Use the operationwise arithmetic model, successful sequential dot products, and $0<u<1$ with $(\max(m,n)-1)u<1$. Define
$$g_k=\frac{1+6u}{1-(k-1)u}-1,\qquad F=\|A\|_F,\quad X=\|x\|_2,\quad Y=\|y\|_2.$$
For $\widehat v=\operatorname{fl}(Ax)$ and $\widehat w=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat v-y)$, put $V=g_nFX$ and $W=V+u(\|\widehat v\|_2+Y)$. Then
$$\|\widehat w-(Ax-y)\|_2\le W.$$
For a stored real $\lambda>0$, also compute $\widehat z=\operatorname{fl}(A^*\widehat w)$, $\widehat l=\operatorname{fl}(\lambda x)$ and $\widehat r=\operatorname{fl}(\widehat z+\widehat l)$, rounding scalar multiplication componentwise. The exact intended normal residual $r=A^*(Ax-y)+\lambda x$ satisfies
$$\|\widehat r-r\|_2\le\rho:=FW+g_mF\|\widehat w\|_2+u\lambda X+u(\|\widehat z\|_2+\|\widehat l\|_2).$$
Norms in these certificates mean exact norms or certified upper bounds. Uncontrolled rounding of the certificate itself is not authorized. The linear bound applies columnwise to certify $\|I-AB\|_2\le\|I-AB\|_F$ from stored basis-solve columns $B$.
ex-subnormal-and-overflow-range-failure:
## Statement

Use binary64 and the no-subnormal success policy. Put N_min=2^-1022 and the least positive subnormal 2^-1074. Inputs N_min and -(N_min+2^-1074) are normal, but their exact sum is -2^-1074, so the only tree sum in pairwise summation returns range-failure. Also N_max+N_max overflows at the root and returns range-failure. These are policy branches, not claims that IEEE hardware lacks gradual underflow.
ex-neumaier-recovers-low-order-term-afte:
## Statement

In binary64 RNE sum (1,2^-53,-1). Ordinary left-to-right summation rounds 1+2^-53 to 1 by ties-to-even, then returns zero after adding -1. Neumaier step 2 gives s_1=1, t_2=1, q_2=0, a_2=2^-53, c_2=2^-53; step 3 gives t_3=0, q_3=1, a_3=0, c_3=2^-53. The final result is 2^-53, the exact sum. The finite error identity accounts for each branch correction and the final rounding.
ex-rounded-cholesky-two-by-two-residual:
## Statement

In binary64 round-to-nearest, ties-to-even, let
$$A=\begin{pmatrix}1&1/2\\1/2&1\\\end{pmatrix}.$$
For every nonzero real $v=(v_1,v_2)^T$,
$$v^TAv=(v_1+v_2/2)^2+3v_2^2/4>0,$$
so $A$ is positive definite. The rounded recurrence gives
$\widehat l_{11}=1$, $\widehat l_{21}=1/2$, $p_2=3/4$ exactly, and
$\widehat l_{22}=\operatorname{fl}(\sqrt{3/4})$. Since $\sqrt3/2$ is irrational and every binary64 number is rational, $\widehat l_{22}^2\ne3/4$. Therefore
$$E=\widehat L\widehat L^T-A= \begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&\widehat l_{22}^2-3/4\end{pmatrix}\ne0.$$
The successful factor satisfies the backward bound, but its residual is not zero.
ex-full-rank-least-squares-normal-equati:
## Statement

In binary64 RNE take A=((1,1),(0,2^-27)). Its determinant 2^-27 is nonzero. The exact Gram matrix is A^T A=((1,1),(1,1+2^-54)). The spacing above 1 is 2^-52, so the midpoint is 1+2^-53; 1+2^-54 lies strictly below it and rounds to 1. Thus the formed Gram matrix has equal rows and is singular. Reduced QR works directly on A and avoids forming this rounded Gram matrix; the computed stability statement remains conditional on its own hypotheses.
ex-ill-conditioned-design-stability-vers:
## Statement

Let A=diag(1,2^-40), with condition number 2^40. For b=(1,0)^T the unique solution is x=(1,0)^T; for b-tilde=(1,2^-40)^T it is x-tilde=(1,1)^T. The relative data change is 2^-40 while the relative solution change is 1. Thus backward stability does not imply small forward error for an ill-conditioned design.
